newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end at 7-yr high on constructions.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end at 7-yr high on constructions.

text.p: Strong buying in recently lagging constructions pushed Taiwan stocks to a seven-year high close on Friday despite a liquidity squeeze and the government's efforts to cool the red-hot bourse, brokers said.
The index again challenged resistance at 9,000 points and spiked to 9,004.18 points before closing at 8,984.59, a gain of 112.83 points or 1.27 percent.
That surpassed Wednesday's 8,956.41 close. The index has not closed higher since ending at 9,292.37 on April 30, 1990.
Friday's tunrover sizzling at T$182 billion, but still well below Thursday's T$232.2 billion.
Turnover had spiked to an all-time high T$251 billion on June 19 as funds gushed into the rejuvenated market.
Brokers said persistently tight liquidity in the banking system and the government's recent cool-off moves did not depress the bullish stock market sentiment.

They said banking system's tight liquidity mainly affected short-term investors, rather than those who aimed at longer-term investment. At 0400 GMT, the overnight interbank rate had surged into double digits at 10.461 percent, a 21-month high.
After days of unheeded persuasion, the central bank said on Friday morning it was taking action by injecting funds.
Keeping up its tough talk, the central bank also vowed to keep a close eye on liquidity flows in the banking system.
"Investors know the government wants to cool the market's temperature, but they don't think it would like to see a big correction," said Ting Kong Securities' analyst Tsao Chung-ping.

With bellwether electronics entering another correction, recent laggard constructions outperformed other shares to soar 6.01 percent on growing expectations that their eight-year slump was finally coming to an end. Ever Fortune surged the daily seven percent limit to T$35.1.
